original.statement: The istio-cni Helm chart now includes a seLinuxOptions configuration value that can be set to work around SELinux constraints on platforms like OpenShift.

of.needed: whether the cluster platform (e.g. OpenShift) enforces SELinux constraints on hostPath volumes used by istio-cni-node pods

corrected.statement: A new value `seLinuxOptions` was added to the istio-cni chart. Exposed environments are those running on platforms with SELinux constraints on hostPath volumes (e.g. OpenShift) that do not set `seLinuxOptions.type`; there the istio-cni-node pods may fail to start. Environments that set `seLinuxOptions.type` to `spc_t` appear safe.

decision.reason: [ev-117557f906cd] says pods may fail to start only on some platforms (e.g. OpenShift) whose SELinux constraints affect hostPath volumes, and only when `seLinuxOptions.type` is not set to `spc_t`. The proposed condition, `seLinuxOptions` unset, would flag every istio-cni install that does not use the new value, including ones on platforms without these SELinux constraints, so it is too broad. No static input shows whether a platform enforces these SELinux constraints, so exposure should combine the unset `seLinuxOptions.type` with an undecidable platform condition. Environments that set the type to `spc_t` touch the subject but appear safe.
